content: Sulindac is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that may increase the risk of heart attack or stroke compared to individuals who do not take NSAIDs. These cardiovascular events can occur without warning and may be fatal. The risk is higher in individuals who use NSAIDs for extended periods. Seek emergency medical attention immediately if you experience symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness on one side of the body, or slurred speech. Sulindac should not be taken immediately before or after coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery. Sulindac and other NSAIDs can cause serious gastrointestinal complications, including ulcers, bleeding, or perforations in the stomach or intestines. These issues can occur at any time during treatment, often without warning, and may be life-threatening. The risk is higher in individuals who use NSAIDs long-term, are older, have poor overall health, or consume large amounts of alcohol. Notify your doctor if you are taking medications such as anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), aspirin, other NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen), or oral steroids (e.g., prednisone). Also, inform your doctor if you have a history of stomach or intestinal ulcers, bleeding disorders, or other gastrointestinal conditions. If you experience symptoms such as stomach pain, heartburn, vomiting blood or material resembling coffee grounds, blood in the stool, or black, tarry stools, stop taking sulindac and contact your doctor immediately. Sulindac is prescribed to alleviate pain, tenderness, swelling, and stiffness associated with osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. It is also used to treat shoulder pain caused by bursitis or tendinitis and to relieve gouty arthritis. Sulindac works by inhibiting the production of substances in the body that cause pain, fever, and inflammation. Sulindac is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken twice daily with food. It is important to take the medication at the same times each day and follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not take more or less than the prescribed dose. While sulindac helps manage arthritis symptoms, it does not cure the condition. It may take a week or longer to experience the full benefits of the medication. In some cases, sulindac is used to reduce the number of polyps in the colon and rectum in patients with familial adenomatous polyposis. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of this treatment with your doctor. Before starting sulindac, inform your doctor if you are allergic to sulindac, aspirin, or other NSAIDs, or if you have any other medication allergies. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially those mentioned in the warning section. Notify your doctor if you have a history of asthma, nasal polyps, kidney stones, swelling in the extremities, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Sulindac should be avoided during the later stages of pregnancy. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking sulindac. Continue your normal diet unless otherwise directed by your doctor. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember, unless it is close to the time for your next dose. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Sulindac may cause mild side effects, including headache, dizziness, nervousness, diarrhea, constipation, gas, or ringing in the ears. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects may include unexplained weight gain, fever, chills, cough, sweating, flushing, muscle or joint pain, chest pain, blisters, rash, itching, hives, swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, hoarseness, pale skin, rapid heartbeat, unusual bleeding or bruising, fatigue, loss of appetite, upper right abdominal pain, flu-like symptoms, yellowing of the skin or eyes, discolored or bloody urine, back pain, painful urination, or vision problems. If you experience any of these severe side effects, stop taking sulindac and contact your doctor immediately. Store sulindac in its original container, tightly sealed, at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Keep it out of reach of children. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In case of an overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call emergency services at 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include loss of consciousness, fainting, dizziness, blurred vision, upset stomach, or decreased urination. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
